entries.title: Agents draft learned skills again, and admit when memory is off
entries.summary: Skill drafts from multi-tool runs were silently failing: a reasoning model spent its whole budget thinking, and the database rejected learned skills after a later migration. Both are fixed, so drafts reach the review queue on /settings/memory again. With memory switched off, an agent now tells you it cannot remember instead of promising to.

entries.title: Agents now identify themselves to the sites they fetch
entries.summary: Pages fetched by agent tools now carry a Web Bot Auth signature, so sites can tell a three.ws agent from an anonymous scraper and let it through. The public key is published at three.ws/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory, and the directory response is itself signed.

entries.title: Context7, Hugging Face and Exa connect without a key
entries.summary: These three integrations only use a key to raise rate limits, and the connect dialog said so, but connecting without one left the server stuck at "Waiting for sign-in" with no tools, so the agent got nothing. They now connect straight away with their read tools on, and you can still paste a key later. Hugging Face's four tools (repo search, repo details, the Hub file browser and whoami) were also all treated as able to change data, so none started on; they are read-only and now start on. A connection that needs you (an expired sign-in, a failed refresh, tools to review) now opens on its own with the fix in view, and stays closed once you collapse it. The primary buttons on the page also show a hover in the dark theme.

entries.title: Every agent wallet is in every custody attestation again
entries.summary: The six-hourly custody snapshot read wallet balances one at a time and ran out of time partway through the fleet, so some epochs covered as few as 400 of 1,063 wallets and the owners of the rest had no inclusion proof to check on /proof that epoch. Balances are now read 100 accounts per call, which covers the whole fleet in seconds. The public /integrity page also stopped logging a console error on every load, and its attestation history table now scrolls cleanly on phones instead of running the columns together.

entries.title: Fewer Solana RPC calls from the agent index and the creator-claims tools
entries.summary: The first full day of per-route RPC accounting showed two callers spending almost a third of our Solana RPC quota. The agent index re-read every agent every 90 minutes even though most have been quiet for weeks; it now re-checks active agents every 20 minutes (more often than before) and quiet ones every four hours, about half the reads. The creator-claims tools on the MCP server now stop at the first transaction a node has not caught up on, read at most 12 new transactions per poll, and share one answer across rapid repeat polls. Fewer wasted calls leaves more quota for payments and the pages people are actually looking at. The status page now judges the agent index by how far it is behind its own schedule.

entries.title: Finished Coin Wars show up in the world ticker and on the chart screen
entries.summary: A finished war now adds a row to the activity ticker for everyone in the room, and a win for the community flashes a band on the chart-screen jumbotron. The result is reported once per match even when the portal poll, the return link and the feed all see it, and only this coin's wars are shown.

entries.title: Onchain viewer recognizes the real SPL Memo v1 program
entries.summary: The /onchain viewer and the Solana Memo Media MCP listed SPL Memo v1 under an address that is not a valid Solana key, so a v1 memo that an RPC did not tag as spl-memo was skipped. Both now use the real program, Memo1UhkJRfHyvLMcVucJwxXeuD728EqVDDwQDxFMNo, and a test checks that every recognized memo program is a real 32-byte key.

entries.title: three-ws/agent output tokens now cost $3 per million
entries.summary: The three-ws/agent model on /api/v1/chat/completions now charges $3.00 per million output tokens, up from $2.00. Input stays at $0.50 per million. The old output rate was below what our paid fallback model costs us, so a busy hour could sell those tokens at a loss. The new rate covers it with margin, and a test now fails if a model change would put the price below cost again. API keys, agent wallet funding and pay-per-request over x402 all use the same rate. Live prices are always at GET /api/v1/models.

entries.summary: Teach an agent from Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF and Outlook files: supported formats and how each is chunked, limits, how chat cites the source, privacy, deletion, and the upload, search and delete API.

entries.title: Docs · Create a 3D model from a Teams or Copilot chat
entries.summary: The Teams app's Create a 3D model action and forge bot command: a real free-lane generation on an Adaptive Card that refreshes for the requester and updates for the whole chat when the model is ready, with Open in 3D, Download GLB and Make a variation.

entries.title: Docs · Creation descriptions (Florence-2)
entries.summary: How every 3D creation gets a caption, detailed caption and tags from Florence-2: the describe queue, the cron, tag rules, owner tag edits, search, page meta and alt text, the backfill script and measured cost.

entries.title: Docs · Enterprise sign-in and SCIM (Microsoft Entra ID)
entries.summary: Sign in with Microsoft for work, school and personal accounts, claiming your organisation's Entra tenant so colleagues join your team, and step-by-step SCIM provisioning from Microsoft Entra ID with the supported filters, PATCH shapes and limits.

entries.title: Docs · Review a 3D model together in a meeting (Live Share)
entries.summary: The three.ws review stage for Teams meetings: follow the presenter's camera, presence, laser pointers, synced comment pins with markdown export and animation sync over Live Share, plus the sideload path, privacy and bundle size.

entries.summary: Export any three.ws model as a PowerPoint slide with an interactive 3D object, and the three.ws 3D Models add-in: the Office-safe GLB pass, the am3d:model3d slide, the limits PowerPoint imposes and how to sideload the add-in.

entries.title: Docs · three.ws on the Microsoft agent stack

entries.title: Docs · TRELLIS.2 Lab
entries.summary: How the TRELLIS.2 Lab works: every parameter and its default, the presets and where their speeds come from, the compare view and share links, the rerunnable production benchmark, how we run Microsoft Research's model on Cloud Run, and the citation.

entries.title: Docs · Trust center
entries.summary: How the three.ws trust center, subprocessor list and security.txt are sourced from the code, and the rules for keeping every claim cited.

entries.summary: Turn any Forge model into blocks and download a Bedrock structure pack: height, block palettes, solid or hollow, texture-sampled colors, loading it with a structure block or /function, limits, the API and the CLI. Not an official Minecraft product.

entries.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Connector Settings
entries.summary: Connect a three.ws account to your organization's Microsoft 365 tenant with admin consent, index your agents, Forge models and avatars for Microsoft Search and Copilot, choose who can see them, watch sync status, run a full re-sync, and disconnect.

entries.title: Open a web+threews link
entries.summary: Where web+threews: links from Windows, Teams, Outlook and documents land: a valid agent, model or forge link opens straight away, and anything else is explained.

entries.title: Review stage (Microsoft Teams meetings)
entries.summary: Review a 3D model together in a Microsoft Teams meeting: follow the presenter's camera, point with live lasers, pin comments on the mesh, export them as markdown and keep animation in sync.

entries.title: Subprocessors
entries.summary: Every third party that processes data for three.ws: purpose, data categories, region and the file that calls it.

entries.title: three.ws 3D Models (PowerPoint add-in)
entries.summary: The three.ws task pane inside PowerPoint: sign in to insert one of your 3D models as an interactive slide, or describe a model and generate it free, then rotate it in your presentation.

entries.title: three.ws and Microsoft
entries.summary: three.ws and Microsoft have announced a partnership, and three.ws is live on Microsoft Marketplace. Watch Microsoft open source run in the product: TRELLIS image-to-3D creations, on-device speech to text through ONNX Runtime Web, and a real agent card drawn with Adaptive Cards, plus the honest status of every Microsoft surface.

entries.title: three.ws in the Edge sidebar
entries.summary: A narrow layout for the browser sidebar: chat with your default agent, turn a prompt into a 3D model, and reopen your recent models next to any page.

entries.title: TRELLIS.2 Lab: Every Parameter of Microsoft Research's Image-to-3D Model
entries.summary: Run Microsoft Research's open TRELLIS.2 image-to-3D model with every parameter exposed: voxel resolution, seed, texture size, face budget and per-stage sampler steps and guidance. Inspect the GLB in texture, wireframe and normal views with real mesh stats, and compare it side by side with another engine on the same photo through a shareable link.

entries.title: Trust center
entries.summary: How three.ws hosts, encrypts, retains and deletes data, which AI providers see prompts, and an honest compliance status, each answer linked to the code that proves it.

entries.title: 3D generation no longer fails while our own GPU worker is busy
entries.summary: Text and photo to 3D in Forge, the GPT forge and the ChatGPT app could fail with Could not generate the model right now even though the three.ws TRELLIS GPU worker had room for the job. A busy worker answers its health check slowly, the router read that as down, and when the outside lanes were also unavailable nothing was left to try. Forge now gives every remaining engine a chance before it gives up, including a worker that only looked down because it was busy, so the job is queued instead of refused.

entries.title: A trust center with security answers that link to the code
entries.summary: three.ws/trust explains where three.ws runs, how data is encrypted, how people and apps sign in, who has admin access, what is logged, how long each kind of data is kept and the job that deletes it, how agent wallet custody works, which AI providers can see prompts (with each provider's own published terms quoted), and how incidents and vulnerability reports are handled. Every answer links to the file in the open-source code that proves it, and the compliance table says plainly what is in place, in progress and not pursued. three.ws/trust/subprocessors lists every third party that processes data, with a filter. Expired sessions, old sign-in nonces and year-old widget views are now actually deleted, as the privacy policy says.

entries.title: An accessibility statement, a full WCAG 2.2 AA conformance report, and fixes for every serious barrier found
entries.summary: three.ws now publishes an accessibility statement at /accessibility. It sets out our commitment, rates the site against WCAG 2.2 Level AA, lists the known gaps with a workaround for each, and tells you how to report a barrier. Behind it is a conformance report in the VPAT 2.x format covering all 56 Level A and AA criteria. Every core page was checked with axe in both themes at desktop and phone width, walked with the keyboard alone, read with the Orca screen reader, zoomed to 400% and viewed in forced colours. All 104 serious or critical issues found are fixed. Among them: 3D views now have names and keyboard orbit, collapsed menus no longer swallow focus, every search field and sign-in field shows a clear focus ring, the home desktop and agent embeds have a main landmark, and invisible controls no longer take focus.

entries.title: An official .NET SDK for three.ws, ready for Unity
entries.summary: C# developers can now use three.ws from one typed library, ThreeWs.Sdk. It generates 3D models from text or images on every Forge lane and downloads the GLB. It also searches the free asset catalog, rigs meshes, streams agent chat and lists MCP tools. It runs on .NET 8 and .NET Standard 2.1, so it works in ASP.NET Core services and in Unity games, and a Unity sample spawns a generated model with glTFast. Every call can be cancelled. Failed requests retry safely, and errors carry the API's error code. The NuGet release is pending.

entries.title: Detailed 3D models no longer fall back to a plain mesh mid-generation
entries.summary: Some requests for a textured model finished as an untextured one. The job was still running on one server, but another server checking on it read an outdated status, decided the job was dead, and handed it to a faster lane without textures. Job status is now always read fresh, so the textured model you asked for is the one you get. The fix covers TRELLIS, TRELLIS.2, Modly, Hunyuan3D and TripoSG.

entries.title: Export any Forge model as a Minecraft: Bedrock structure pack
entries.summary: The Forge download menu has a new Minecraft: Bedrock option. It turns your model into blocks, shows a live 3D block preview, and downloads a .mcpack you open in Bedrock and place with a structure block or one /function command. Pick the height (16 to 128 blocks), which blocks to use (all, concrete, wool, terracotta, builder or colorful), solid or hollow, and optional dithering. Colors come from the model's texture at every block, and dark textures are brightened automatically so a steel knight does not come out as coal. Builds wider than one structure block are split into tiles that the function places together. Not an official Minecraft product; not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft.

entries.title: Find 3D models by what is in them
entries.summary: Every finished 3D creation is now described from its poster by Florence-2 on our own GPU: a short caption, a detailed caption and tags. Model search matches those captions and tags, so a model forged from a photo with no written prompt still turns up when you search for what it shows, like "bicycle wheel". Model pages use the detailed caption as their description and as alt text for the 3D viewer and share images, and list the tags as chips that open a search for similar models. Creators can add, remove or clear the tags on their own models.

entries.title: Find your three.ws agents and 3D models in Microsoft 365 Copilot
entries.summary: A Microsoft 365 administrator can now connect a three.ws account to their organization from Settings > Microsoft 365. Your public agents, Forge models and avatars are indexed into the tenant, so people in the organization find them in Microsoft Search and can ask Microsoft 365 Copilot about them, with links back to three.ws. You choose who sees them: everyone in the organization except guests, one Entra group, or only you. Changes reach Microsoft every 15 minutes, items you delete or make private are removed, Microsoft's throttling is respected, and a Full re-sync button resends everything at once. Disconnecting deletes the index from the tenant. It goes live once the three.ws Microsoft app is approved for the two Graph permissions it needs.

entries.title: Generate a 3D model without leaving a Teams chat
entries.summary: The three.ws Teams app can now make 3D models inside a conversation. Choose Create a 3D model from the compose box or a message's menu, or message the bot forge followed by a description. A card shows your prompt, who asked and where the job really is (GPU waking up, queued, rendering), and it turns into the finished model when it is ready: a rendered preview, Open in 3D in the three.ws viewer, Download GLB, and Make a variation for a new take on the same prompt. If a job fails, the card says what went wrong and offers Try again. It runs on the same free text-to-3D lane as the three.ws MCP tools.

entries.title: Give a Semantic Kernel or Microsoft Agent Framework agent 3D generation
entries.summary: Two new plugins, threews-semantic-kernel for Python and ThreeWs.SemanticKernel for .NET, give an agent six functions on three.ws: generate a textured 3D model from text and wait for it, check a generation, search thousands of free ready-made props, characters and motion clips, list your agents, search the public agent directory and message an agent. Each also attaches the free MCP 3D studio in one line. Python and .NET Agent Framework samples pick the prop a scene needs, check the catalog and return a real downloadable model, and a quickstart attaches the studio to a Foundry agent. No account or key is needed except to list your own agents. Both packages ship with live tests against the real API and go up on PyPI and NuGet with the owner's publish.

entries.title: Microsoft Marketplace leads land in three.ws with a reply ready to send
entries.summary: When someone asks for a demo, starts a trial or installs three.ws from Microsoft Marketplace, the lead now arrives in three.ws within seconds. It is stored once even if Microsoft retries, the team is notified once, and a reply is drafted from the offer and the person's own message. Nothing is sent automatically: the team reviews the draft, sends it themselves and marks the lead contacted. Do-not-contact requests get no reply, and personal details are deleted on a fixed schedule.

entries.title: Open 3D files from File Explorer and keep your agent in the Edge sidebar
entries.summary: The installed three.ws app now opens .glb, .gltf and .vrm files you double-click in Windows File Explorer, reading them on your PC with nothing uploaded unless you press Save to account. web+threews: links from Teams, Outlook or a document open the right agent, model or text to 3D prompt, and a link that is broken or unsafe is explained instead of followed. A second launch reuses the window you already have open, the site header doubles as the title bar when the title bar is hidden, and a new narrow layout at /sidebar puts agent chat, quick text to 3D and your recent models in the Microsoft Edge sidebar.

entries.title: Put an interactive 3D model on a PowerPoint slide in one click
entries.summary: Choose PowerPoint in the Forge export menu, in Forge Studio or on any model page and you get a ready slide: the prompt as the title and the model as a real PowerPoint 3D object you can drag to rotate in a slideshow, animate with Morph and resize like a picture. Every model is prepared for Office first: compressed geometry is decoded, textures become PNG or JPEG at up to 2048 px, rigs and animation are kept, and a rendered poster shows in viewers without 3D. The new three.ws 3D Models add-in for PowerPoint does the same from inside your presentation: sign in with your three.ws account to insert one of your models, or describe one and generate it free. The add-in can be sideloaded today and its AppSource listing is pending review.

entries.title: Put interactive 3D models in a Power BI report
entries.summary: three.ws 3D Models is a custom visual for Power BI reports. Bind a column of three.ws model ids or GLB links and it shows one model you can orbit, a grid, or a turntable gallery for larger sets. Measures can colour and size each model, a click cross-filters the rest of the report, selections elsewhere highlight the matching models, and tooltips show any fields you add. The format pane covers background, lighting, layout, auto-rotate, colour mode and labels, and the visual supports the keyboard, high-contrast themes and the context menu. It downloads models only from three.ws. The package is built and tested against real production models, and the AppSource submission is next.

entries.title: Ready-made Power Automate flows for the three.ws connector
entries.summary: The three.ws Power Platform connector now comes with four flow templates: turn a new SharePoint list item into a 3D model and post it to Teams, email a model to whoever fills in a Microsoft Forms request, send a daily digest of your agents and the newest public ones, and let a Teams channel ask your three.ws agent questions. A Copilot Studio agent sample uses the same five actions. Every action now declares the exact response it returns, checked against the live service, and the connector is packaged for Microsoft certification (pending review).

entries.title: Review a 3D model together in a Microsoft Teams meeting
entries.summary: Add three.ws to a Teams meeting and share a model to the meeting stage, and everyone in the call looks at the same mesh. Press Present and your camera drives everyone's view; anyone who orbits away gets a one-click jump back to the presenter. Each person's initials show who is watching, and their pointer appears on everyone else's screen as a coloured laser on the exact spot of the model. Click the mesh to pin a comment, and the pin appears for the whole meeting; export every pin as markdown when you are done. Clip, play state and playhead stay in sync, so everyone sees the same frame. Pick from your own models, the featured library or a pasted link. Opened outside a meeting, the stage works for one person and explains how to review together. three.ws keeps no meeting content unless you export the pins.

entries.title: See Microsoft technology running live on three.ws/microsoft
entries.summary: The new Microsoft page shows Microsoft open source at work inside three.ws: 3D models people made with TRELLIS, speech to text that runs entirely in your browser so the audio never leaves your device, and a real agent's card drawn with Adaptive Cards that you can copy into the designer. It also lists every Microsoft surface three.ws is built for, from Marketplace and Teams to Power Platform, Edge and VS Code, with an honest status for each and what you can do there today.

entries.title: Sign in with Microsoft, and let Microsoft Entra ID manage your team
entries.summary: Anyone can now sign in with a work, school or personal Microsoft account, and link it to an existing account from Settings. Team owners can claim their organisation's Microsoft Entra tenant with an admin sign-in, so colleagues are offered the team (or join automatically) the first time they sign in. Entra ID can provision people and groups over SCIM: when someone leaves or is unassigned, their team access ends and their sessions from that organisation are signed out. Setup takes a few minutes and every change is logged on the team page.

entries.title: Teach your agent from Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF and Outlook files
entries.summary: Open the Knowledge tab on an agent's edit page and drop in a handbook, a pitch deck, a price list, a policy PDF or an email. Each file shows its own upload progress, then is read with Microsoft MarkItDown on our own hardened converter, split into sections, one per slide, sheet or email, and indexed for search. From the next message the agent answers from those files and names the one it used. A test box shows exactly which passages it would draw on and streams a real answer beside them. Delete a file and everything derived from it goes with it; the original file is never stored. Up to 50 files of 25 MB each per agent.

entries.title: three.ws in GitHub Copilot Chat for VS Code
entries.summary: Version 0.3.0 of the three.ws 3D extension for VS Code works inside GitHub Copilot Chat. Type @threews /forge and a description to generate a free 3D model, with the studio's real progress streamed into the chat. It ends with buttons to open the model in the viewer or save the GLB to your workspace. /find searches the free asset catalog, /rig rigs a GLB, and /embed inserts a pinned <agent-3d> snippet into the open file. In agent mode, Copilot can call five three.ws tools by itself: generate a model, check a job, find an asset, and inspect or optimize a local GLB. It asks first before using GPU time or writing a file. The free three.ws Studio MCP server is registered automatically, and one command connects your account server. Needs VS Code 1.101 or newer.

entries.title: three.ws now tells Bing, and through it Copilot, about every new page within minutes
entries.summary: When you publish an agent, an avatar, a creation, a widget or a profile, three.ws now announces it to Bing over IndexNow within minutes instead of waiting for the next crawl, so it can show up in Copilot answers and Windows search the same day. Changes and removals are announced too, and a page that goes private is withdrawn without ever being sent while it was hidden. The sitemaps now list every public agent, avatar, creation, widget and profile from the database with the real date each one last changed, and creations made from the same prompt no longer flood search with near-identical pages. Search engines also read richer pages: public profiles have their own page with your name, bio and work instead of a blank shell, same-named agents and avatars are told apart by their creator, and the FAQ answers search engines see on the feature pages are now exactly the ones you see.

entries.title: TRELLIS.2 Lab presets now show when a setting is failing on production
entries.summary: The preset cards in the TRELLIS.2 Lab now read the first real TRELLIS.2 production runs. Fast draft shows its measured time, about a minute end to end. Balanced and Maximum detail now say "Failing on production" and give the number of failed runs, instead of a vague "Not measured yet", so you know to start with Fast draft. When a run fails, its error panel no longer shows a stray "null" beside Retry or a doubled full stop.

entries.title: TRELLIS.2 Lab: every parameter of Microsoft Research's image-to-3D model
entries.summary: A new lab at /lab/trellis2 runs TRELLIS.2 with all of its controls in your hands: voxel resolution, seed, texture size, face budget, and the steps and guidance of each of its three sampler stages. Every control shows its default and a plain-language explanation. Pick Fast draft, Balanced or Maximum detail; their speed labels come from real production runs, not estimates. Inspect the result in texture, wireframe or normal view, with triangle count, texture resolution and file size read from the model itself. Run a second engine on the same photo to compare the two side by side, and share the pair with one link. The page credits Microsoft Research, with the citation, the MIT license and how we run it.

entries.title: Turn a photo into a 3D diorama
entries.summary: Diorama can now rebuild a scene you photographed. Click From a photo, or drop or paste an image onto the page. An AI set designer reads the photo, boxes every separate object, and estimates how far away and how big each one is and what it rests on. Each object is then turned into its own 3D model from its crop of your photo, so it keeps its real shape and colour. Objects that are partly hidden are built from a description instead. The pieces drop into place where they stood in the picture, and a laptop sits on top of the desk it was on, not beside it. A small copy of your photo stays in the corner with a live box for every object, and hovering a piece highlights its box. Pieces built from your photo carry a small picture mark. The camera frames the objects, not the whole island, so the scene reads at the size it had in the photo. Photo worlds save, share, remix and export like any other world. The scene reader also got more reliable: when one free vision route is busy it now tries the next one instead of giving up, and an end-of-life model was replaced with its current successor.

entries.title: Docs · Robinhood Crypto connector
entries.summary: Connect your own Robinhood Crypto Trading API key to three.ws, set hard per-order and daily spend caps, and let agents quote, preview and place crypto orders through REST or MCP: the two-step confirm flow, cap reservation, error codes and security model.

entries.title: Robinhood Crypto Connector Settings
entries.summary: Connect your own Robinhood Crypto account with its Crypto Trading API key, generate the Ed25519 key pair in your browser, set hard per-order and daily spend caps for agent orders, pause trading, see holdings and the order ledger, and disconnect.

entries.title: Agent run replays show the code your agent ran
entries.summary: On an agent's Runs tab, each execute_code, terminal and file step now shows the program, what it printed, its exit code and duration, and download links for the files it wrote, right in the step instead of behind a Details fold. The sandbox settings page empty state now tells you to ask your agent to run code.

entries.title: Buy a skill bundle straight from an agent's marketplace page
entries.summary: An agent's Capabilities tab now shows its published skill bundles above the individual skills: what is included, the bundle price in $THREE or USDC, and how much you save against buying each skill alone (computed from the agent's real list prices, never estimated). Buy opens the usual payment modal with wallet or Solana Pay QR checkout, and once the payment is verified on-chain every skill in the bundle shows as owned. This also fixes bundle checkout itself, which failed with a server error whenever no platform fee applied and quoted the wrong split when one did, and now answers 'already owned' instead of opening a second purchase.

entries.title: Connect your Robinhood Crypto account and let agents trade inside your caps
entries.summary: You can now connect your own Robinhood Crypto account to three.ws with a Crypto Trading API key, generating the key pair right in your browser. Set a per-order and a daily spend cap, and your agents can read holdings, quote pairs and preview orders. An order is only placed after you approve its confirm table, every buy is checked against your caps on the server before it reaches Robinhood, and you can pause trading or disconnect at any time. Crypto pairs only.

entries.title: Every demo surface now opens on the house avatar
entries.summary: The home page, viewer, pricing, features, game NPCs, Pose Studio, Arena, Create Agent and the avatar templates no longer default to a real person's likeness. They start on the house avatar or another house body, and avatars you bring yourself work exactly as before.

entries.title: Forge composer no longer jumps while it loads
entries.summary: The engine picker, the cost caption and the Enhance button now hold their space from the first frame, so the page stops shifting under your cursor on a first visit. Measured layout shift on the Forge page fell from 0.11 to 0.41 down to 0.05 to 0.28 across phone and desktop widths.

entries.title: Multiplayer worlds hold together across several servers
entries.summary: Players who land on a different server than the one hosting their world are now bridged to it, so a crowd can be spread over several servers without anyone being cut off. Measured on a two-server test fleet backed by a dedicated shared Redis: 200 players across 4 coin worlds joined with no failures or dropped connections, and every one of 186000 chat deliveries arrived. The live world server is unchanged until its next deploy.

entries.title: One button style across Brain, Flow, Home, Avatar Studio and agent pages
entries.summary: Buttons on the Brain, Flow map, First Meet, Home studio cards, Avatar Studio and agent detail pages now use the shared button component, so hover, pressed, keyboard focus and disabled states look and behave the same everywhere.

entries.title: Places search keeps answering when the public map servers stall
entries.summary: The paid and free places search returned an error for every caller when the public OpenStreetMap servers it reads were overloaded at the same time. It now asks several map servers in parallel and takes the first answer, remembers recent results so repeat searches return instantly, and if every server is down it serves the last real answer it saw, clearly marked as stale with the time it was fetched.

entries.title: Pump.fun claim lookups stop draining the shared Solana RPC budget
entries.summary: The pump.fun MCP tools that list a creator's fee claims were the largest single consumer of the platform's Solana RPC quota, because a busy poller rescanned every transaction on every call and retried each one when the providers were throttling. A claims scan now skips transactions that failed on-chain, stops at the first throttled read, reads a bounded number of new transactions per call, and shares a fresh answer between rapid repeat polls. Results cut short say so with an incomplete flag and fill in on the next call, so payments and balance reads keep their RPC headroom.

entries.title: Restyle Studio states its 18 material presets on the page
entries.summary: The preset count now sits above the preset grid in Restyle Studio, so visitors see how many PBR looks are on offer without reading the page metadata.

entries.title: The agent-3d embed script is 18% smaller
entries.summary: The single-file <agent-3d> embed had grown to 5.8MB because the LiveKit voice session and the on-device speech detector were baked into it, even on pages that never start a voice call. Both now load from the CDN the first time a visitor starts voice, so the script every embedding page downloads is down to 4.8MB. Voice behaves the same once it starts.

entries.title: The site header no longer pushes pages down as it loads
entries.summary: The skip link and the shared header now hold their final space from the first paint on every page, and the Forge example prompts sit in fixed cells, so content stops jumping under your cursor while a page loads.

entries.title: The TRELLIS image-to-3D container now runs on A100 and L4 GPUs with no critical vulnerabilities
entries.summary: The container behind our image-to-3D lane, prepared for NVIDIA's NGC Catalog, is now a two-stage build on CUDA 12.6 and Python 3.12. It is 32% smaller (8.4GB instead of 12.3GB), and its security scan went from 70 critical and 1437 high findings to 0 critical and 2 high, both waiting on upstream releases. A real job ran end to end on an NVIDIA A100 and an NVIDIA L4, each producing a textured 3D model, with the code also compiled for Hopper GPUs.

entries.title: Meetup #3 Recap: The Three.ws User Group Back in the World
entries.summary: How the Three.ws User Group's third meetup went, sponsored by IBM Community and held inside the $THREE home town at three.ws/play: the first project-owned user group on IBM Community, the first names on the signature wall, what shipped since August, and what comes next.

entries.title: The Community Meetup #3 recap is up: a wrap on our IBM Community user group's second meetup inside the world
entries.summary: How the Three.ws User Group's third meetup went, sponsored by IBM Community and held inside /play on November 6. three.ws is the first project with its own user group on IBM Community, the new signature wall got its first names, and people kept coming back after the program ended. The post also covers everything shipped since August, the full partner roster, and the next session being planned for late November.

entries.title: Docs · Play lite: the /play world on any device
entries.summary: How /play/lite joins the same live room as the 3D plaza without WebGL: what a lite player can do, when /play hands off automatically, the slow-device offer, and how to verify it locally.

entries.title: Play lite: join the live world from any device
entries.summary: The same live /play world, people, chat, dance-off and signature wall as the 3D plaza, drawn as a live map that runs on any phone or laptop, no graphics card needed.

entries.title: Agent payments on Solana stop stalling on a starved RPC
entries.summary: The background leak scanner was spending a quarter of the platform's daily Solana RPC calls rechecking wallets that never move money, which used up the paid RPC lanes and left agent-to-agent x402 payments waiting on slow public ones. Idle wallets are now checked in a steady rotation while every wallet that actually paid is still checked within ten minutes, so payments at the Agent Exchange settle on the fast lanes again.

entries.title: Card gacha pulls work from wallets that hold SOL
entries.summary: Pulling a card in /play failed with "could not verify" for any wallet holding SOL, and nothing was charged. Collector Crypt has those wallets pay their own network fee, about 0.00001 SOL, and our safety check only allowed the case where Collector Crypt pays it. The check now accepts both while keeping every other rule, adds a cap so the fee can never be inflated, and the confirmation table shows who pays the fee and exactly how much.

entries.title: Every launched coin now gets fresh stats
entries.summary: Launch stats only ever refreshed for the first 20 coins, so most launches showed old numbers or none at all, and their owners never heard when a coin filled its curve. The refresh now works through every coin, oldest data first, and a full pass takes under an hour. Coins that filled long ago are corrected quietly and are not announced as new.

entries.title: Join any /play world from any phone or laptop with Play lite
entries.summary: Devices that can't run the 3D world (no graphics acceleration, an old phone, a locked-down work laptop) now land in Play lite: the same live room drawn as a top-down map. You walk by tapping, chat, react, emote, enter and vote in the dance-off, sign the wall and follow the meetup agenda, and everyone in 3D sees you arrive as an avatar. /play switches over automatically before the 3D engine downloads, a slow device is offered the switch, and Open in 3D takes you back.

entries.title: Large avatars and forge props load again when the edge cache misses
entries.summary: Models over 32 MB (several mixamo avatars and forge props are 38 to 42 MB) failed with an empty server error on a full download whenever the CDN edge did not already hold them, because Cloud Run rejects a buffered response that large. Those downloads now stream, so an avatar or prop in /play no longer depends on the cache being warm.

entries.title: Pages keep working right after a site update
entries.summary: Right after an update, /play could stop on "Couldn't load the world" and other pages could fail the same way, because our network edge kept handing out an old copy of the page that pointed at files the update had removed. Reloading fetched the same old copy, so Try again could not help. Pages now always come fresh from the site, so an update can no longer strand visitors on a dead copy.

entries.title: Paid 3D generation keeps working when outside engines are down
entries.summary: When the outside 3D engines were busy, a paid Forge request could wait over a minute and then fail with a message saying generation was not configured. No one was charged, but no model came back either. Paid requests now fall through to our own GPU worker, the same one that powers the free Forge, and get a job to follow within seconds.

entries.title: Queued 3D and avatar jobs are no longer failed while they wait their turn
entries.summary: On the self-hosted text-to-3D worker, a job waiting behind another could be marked as orphaned a few minutes after submit even though its runner was still alive, which sent the request to a slower fallback or failed it. A worker now trusts its own live record over a lagging storage read, so queued jobs wait and then run.

entries.title: Solana stays responsive for payments when RPC providers throttle
entries.summary: Three background jobs were spending most of the platform's Solana RPC calls: the wallet leak scanner kept grinding through retries while every paid provider was throttled, the treasury refill read agent wallet balances one call at a time, and the pump.fun claims tool re-read the same confirmed transactions on every poll. The scanner now pauses its low-priority wallets until a paid provider is back, balances are read 100 at a time, and each transaction's claim result is remembered, so agent payments and live features keep the RPC capacity they need.

entries.title: The meetup group photo is stamped with the event name every time
entries.summary: The photo screen loaded only when the shutter fired, so on a slow connection the card could open without the event name or arrive late. It now loads during the minute before the shutter, so the group photo is ready the instant it fires.

entries.title: The official three.ws town on /play shows its name and art again
entries.summary: When pump.fun's coin API was unreachable, the pinned OFFICIAL card at the top of the /play lobby lost its identity and read "Unnamed coin" with a blank letter tile. The card now keeps three.ws and its artwork whatever the live refresh returns, and the coin lookup behind it names any Solana coin from its on-chain token metadata while pump.fun is down.

entries.title: The oracle ribbon in /play no longer stalls when its price feed is throttled
entries.summary: When GeckoTerminal throttled the candle refresh behind the Granite Oracle, the first visitor after the cache lapsed waited about 16 seconds. Candle reads now hand back the previous candles after 2.5 seconds and finish the refresh in the background, so the ribbon loads promptly and the next visitor sees fresh data.

entries.title: The Play world holds up on phones, blocked storage and blocked scripts
entries.summary: Every Play button on a touch screen now meets the 44 px target size, the meetup countdown chip sits under the top bar instead of covering Shop, Buy and Friends, the event countdown keeps running when the browser blocks local storage, a blocked locale script no longer stops the world from loading, and the agent exchange no longer downloads the animation list a second time.

entries.title: Auto-rigged legs no longer drag cloth between them
entries.summary: Rigging a character in wide trousers or a skirt used to blend both legs' influence on the cloth between them, so a step or a kick stretched a sheet of fabric from one leg to the other. The rigger now commits every vertex to the leg it actually sits on, with a narrow soft seam at the midline, so each trouser leg moves with its own leg.

entries.title: Autopilot can propose trades, and a trading MCP fills them under the wallet guards
entries.summary: Autopilot gained a trade action. The agent can queue a buy with SOL or a sell of a non-$THREE token, grounded in the memories that motivated it; nothing moves until you confirm, and every fill runs the wallet guards (per-trade cap, daily budget, price-impact breaker, rug firewall) with buys counted against the daily SOL limit. A sell of $THREE is refused. The new @three-ws/trading-mcp quotes, lists positions and fills the same way from any MCP client.

entries.title: Coin Radar now keeps every launch it has ever observed
entries.summary: The launch intelligence behind /radar, /coin-intel and the Oracle coin pages used to be deleted after its retention window with no copy kept, so only the last few days of observed launches existed. Every coin past the window, with its wallet breakdown, outcome, smart-money read and conviction history, is now written to verified cold storage before it leaves the live database, and can be restored by date range.

entries.title: Every animation in the gallery plays again
entries.summary: Opening any of the 469 community clips on /animations showed "Couldn't load this clip's preview", and clips that did load froze in a T-pose at 0.0s once the detail view opened. Community clips now load in the gallery, the Animation Studio and every embed, and the detail view plays each clip from start to finish with a working scrubber.

entries.title: Forge stops dead-ending on engines your region can't use
entries.summary: Picking Hunyuan3D or the free Hunyuan3D / TRELLIS lane on /forge could fail with a bare error, and every retry hit the same wall, because those engines' model licence excludes some regions. Forge now greys those engines out up front with the reason, and if one is still picked it switches to an engine that can take your prompt and says so, with no action needed.

entries.title: Marketplace agent cards show their avatars again
entries.summary: Agent cards on /marketplace were showing only a letter where the avatar should be, because the stored picture was tied to the 3D viewer, which stays hidden until you hover a card. Every card now shows its avatar picture straight away, and hovering still swaps in the live, turning 3D model.

entries.title: New gallery avatars stop getting white hands and the wrong face
entries.summary: Avatars added to the public gallery each minute could come out with flat white hands that did not match the face, a man's card with a woman's face and long hair, or novelty reindeer antlers worn as glasses. Hands and neck now take the same skin tone as the face, hair and clothes always match the avatar's gender, and the antler piece is no longer offered as eyewear.

entries.title: Sell everything an agent bought, or trade any coin by hand
entries.summary: Owners can now exit all of an agent's positions in one reviewed run. The wallet Trade tab has a Sell all that lists every coin the wallet holds, lets you untick what to keep, pick slippage and pause the sniper, then sells one coin at a time with live status, Stop and a retry for anything unsold. The sniper dashboard gets a Sell all for every open position across your agents, and links from each agent to manual trading. Clicking a holding in Trade or Portfolio now loads that coin ready to sell.

entries.summary: Add the free three.ws 3D Studio to your own ChatGPT in about a minute: the exact settings to paste, a live check of the server from your browser, prompts to try and fixes for every setup snag. Text and photos become interactive 3D models and rigged avatars inline in the conversation. No account, no key.

entries.summary: Arm an agent on Oracle calls, watch it, set its guardrails and stop it from any MCP client. Can move real SOL; simulate by default.

entries.summary: How three.ws turns its live Microsoft Marketplace publisher profile into offers: a transactable SaaS listing, Copilot MCP certification, professional services, a Power Platform connector, a Teams app, and the VS Code and Edge stores.

entries.summary: Metered web search, page fetch, document parsing, speech and image tools on one credit balance: prices, the REST and MCP contracts, refunds, idempotency and the SSRF guard.

entries.summary: How a late joiner sees a /play world's last 60 chat lines above a caught-up divider, the cap, expiry and privacy rules for stored lines, and the read-only Board tab that shows a coin's community posts in-world.

entries.summary: The A2A endpoint any agent can call: the Agent Card, the generate-3d-model, validate-model and search-avatars skills, A2A 1.0 and 0.3 JSON-RPC methods, task lifetime, error codes, optional bearer auth, and curl calls that work today.

entries.title: Forge-Off: Daily Themed 3D Contest
entries.summary: A themed creation contest with no account: describe a thing, get a real textured 3D model, publish it, and vote. One board per day, an overall winner, and a standing weekly board between events.

entries.title: Glass
entries.summary: The three.ws web app for Meta Ray-Ban Display. See the agents standing around you, talk to one with a pinch, and hand it off to your phone.

entries.summary: Agents post real-world jobs with a USDC bounty held in escrow on Solana. Accept one, submit proof, and get paid when the poster approves.

entries.summary: The open inference network: community nodes that sell compute into the three.ws queue, their capabilities, uptime and verified earnings.

entries.title: MCP Integrations
entries.summary: Connect your agent to third-party MCP servers: a vetted catalog of 80+ servers (documentation, developer tools, project trackers, CRM, payments, data and more) plus any public HTTPS server by URL. Sign in with OAuth or paste a token, turn tools on per agent grouped by read, write and financial tiers, and review a custom server's tools before anything runs. The agent sees each tool as ext_<name>_<tool>.

entries.title: MCP Tool Access Settings
entries.summary: Choose which three.ws MCP tool groups your agents, connectors and AI clients can call. Turn a group on to unlock its financial tools such as swaps, transfers and launches, or off to hide it everywhere. Every disabled-tool refusal links here.

entries.title: Multichain Launchpad
entries.summary: Launch a coin about an animation, an avatar, a 3D agent or all three on Solana (pump.fun), BNB Chain (four.meme, flap.sh), Base and Robinhood Chain (flap.sh), signed by your agent's wallet or your own, with a live fee quote, a confirmation table and a permanent 3D showcase page for every coin.

entries.title: three.ws agents (Microsoft Teams tab)
entries.summary: The three.ws tab inside Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365: pick one of your agents and talk to it, or generate a 3D model from a prompt, without leaving the meeting or chat.

entries.title: $THREE buyback lanes can no longer sweep the holder-rewards pool
entries.summary: If the rewards wallet is ever the same wallet as the buyback or micro-buy signer, those lanes now refuse to run instead of sweeping the whole rewards pool into the treasury, and the ops health check flags it. A new read-only preflight, npm run token:preflight, validates the treasury and rewards addresses against mainnet and prints the one command that applies them.

entries.title: $THREE purchases and Premium pass payments build correctly for the Token-2022 mint
entries.summary: $THREE is a Token-2022 token, and several Solana payment builders were deriving token accounts under the older token program, which produces a transfer the network rejects. Skill purchases, agent purchases, subscriptions and the Premium data pass now read the token program from the mint and create any missing $THREE account in the same transaction. A new script simulates both the gasless purchase and the Premium payment for a real holder on mainnet without signing or sending anything, and both pass.

entries.title: 3D generation workers accept PNG, JPEG and WEBP only, and say so when an image is refused
entries.summary: Every photo you hand Forge, avatar reconstruction or scene decomposition is now decoded only as PNG, JPEG or WEBP, so a file in any other format never reaches an image parser on the GPU workers. A refused or corrupt image now fails with a clear message naming the three formats instead of a generic worker error. The image library is pinned exactly on every worker, the talking-avatar worker moves to transformers 4.57.6 with bit-identical output, and oversized EXIF blocks are ignored rather than parsed. Takes effect as each worker image is rebuilt.

entries.title: A concierge greets new visitors in the world
entries.summary: A well-dressed concierge near spawn welcomes first-time players once, answers questions about the stations that really exist through the free chat model, and leads a skippable tour of the Intel Kiosk, Signature Wall, wheel and War Portal. During a live event it opens with what is happening.

entries.title: A paid agent skill call whose response was lost can now be collected again without paying twice
entries.summary: When you pay for an agent skill and the connection drops before the answer arrives, asking again with the same Idempotency-Key (or the same payment intent) now returns the stored result, marked replayed, instead of a payment_in_flight error or a second charge. The skill runs once and the author is credited once. A retry with different arguments is refused with idempotency_conflict, a retry while the first call is still running gets idempotency_in_progress with a retry-after, and a call that fails stores nothing so the paid intent can be retried. The 402 challenge and the manifest now advertise the header, the 24 hour window and the replayed field, and the browser x402 client sends one key per call and retries a dropped paid request once on its own.

entries.title: Account status, dashboard links and X posting tools for connected assistants
entries.summary: GET /api/v1/me/status and the get_account_status tool answer what plan you are on, what is left and what is waiting for approval in one call. get_dashboard_urls returns the canonical page links. Agents can now be connected to X, given a posting policy and asked to post through MCP, with review-before-post queuing instead of publishing. Settings shows account status and each agent's X posting state.

entries.title: Add three.ws to your own ChatGPT in about a minute
entries.summary: A new /chatgpt page walks you through adding the free three.ws 3D Studio to ChatGPT: turn on developer mode, create an app with the URL https://three.ws/api/mcp-chatgpt and no authentication, then ask for a model. Text and photos become interactive, textured 3D models and rigged avatars that render inline in the conversation, free and with no account. The page checks the server live from your browser, lists the exact tools ChatGPT gets, and has starter prompts and fixes for every setup snag.

entries.title: Agent memory now knows when a fact was true
entries.summary: Memories carry a validity interval and a source. When something changes (moved cities, new job) the agent saves the new fact as superseding the old one, so recall returns what is true now, as_of asks what was true at an earlier date, and the old version stays as history. The @three-ws/agent-memory SDK gained validFrom, sourceRef, supersedes, asOf and includeHistory, and a benchmark harness scores recall on LoCoMo and LongMemEval.

entries.title: Agent memory recall now understands meaning, not just exact words
entries.summary: An agent whose memory says it prefers dark mode now recalls that when you ask what theme you like. The memory file layer ranks files by embedding similarity through a new signed-in endpoint, POST /api/memory/rank, instead of requiring the whole query to appear verbatim. Results carry a text field and honor a minimum score, so the studio Brain memory node gets usable recalls. If the endpoint is unreachable or embeddings are not configured, recall falls back to the old substring match, so it never fails mid-conversation.

entries.title: Agent payment mandates are pinned to USDC and refuse any other currency
entries.summary: An Intent Mandate lets your agent pay other agents without asking you each time, within a budget. Issuing one with an empty or non-USDC currency used to succeed and quietly turned off the currency check, so a payment in an asset the spend guard cannot price could bypass your per-payment, daily and per-recipient dollar limits. Mandates now accept USDC only, refuse anything else with unsupported_currency, and any mandate signed with a bad currency before this fix is refused when the agent tries to spend under it.

entries.title: Agent sandbox settings
entries.summary: A new Settings page lists every program your agents ran in their sandbox with its output and exit code, lets you download the files it wrote, stop a workspace, and choose which hosts sandboxed code may call.

entries.title: Agent wallet key export and rotation now require the real-funds agreements
entries.summary: Exporting an agent wallet key and confirming a rotate-and-sweep now check that the owner has signed the real-funds agreements, like every other path that moves or releases custodial funds. The rotation preview stays open, devnet is unaffected, and an owner who has not signed can sign and retry with the same re-authentication. Agent wallet provisioning also claims the wallet slot atomically, so two concurrent first requests can no longer replace a key whose address was already handed out.

entries.title: Agents can browse the web toward a goal
entries.summary: Give an agent a goal and a public page and it browses in a real browser you can watch, one validated step at a time. It stays on the allowed sites, never enters passwords or payment details, stops at its step limit, and hands the browser to you the moment you take over. Available in the Browse panel on the agent screen and as the browse_web tool.

entries.title: Agents can lend idle funds on Solana
entries.summary: A new Lend tab in the agent wallet, v1 lending routes and five MCP tools let an agent supply idle USDC to Kamino Lend, see its position, APY and health factor, and withdraw. Every move is simulated first and needs an explicit confirm; an owner-set earn rule keeps idle funds working.

entries.title: Agents on one stage take turns speaking instead of talking over each other
entries.summary: When several <agent-3d> agents share an <agent-stage>, everything they say out loud now goes through one speaking queue, so a cue answered by two agents plays one voice after the other. Lines from someone talking to an agent go first, then answers to a stage-wide cue, then idle chatter, and nobody is cut off mid-sentence. A voice that fails or never finishes is skipped so the scene keeps moving, and removing or pausing an agent cancels its waiting lines. Pages can follow who holds the floor with the new stage:speaking-change event, queue their own lines with stage.speak(), and say() now resolves to the reply. Agents also join the stage the moment their brain boots, which is what gives them say_to_agent and observe_agents; before this, a reply from say_to_agent always came back empty. The two-agents example shows the floor live.

entries.title: Agents SDK routes are all real
entries.summary: Every @three-ws/agents method now calls a mounted /api/v1 route: account usage, budget, ledger, integrations and link codes, six market intel reads (price, top movers, RSI/EMA/MACD indicators, signals, anomalies, macro) and read-only agent wallet balance and history. Swap execution and transfers stay out of the API by design. The package ships a route-parity test, a full transport, error and SSE suite, and runnable examples.

entries.title: Agents sign their web requests
entries.summary: Fetches made by three.ws agents through the tool gateway and the screen caster now carry a Web Bot Auth signature, and the matching public key directory is served at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory, so sites can verify and rate-limit three.ws agents instead of blocking them.

entries.title: Agents speak AG-UI to CopilotKit and assistant-ui
entries.summary: POST /api/agent/run?protocol=ag-ui now streams the run as AG-UI events (run, text message and tool call lifecycle, plus avatar embodiment cues as CUSTOM events), so CopilotKit, assistant-ui and LangChain front ends can drive a three.ws agent with no adapter. The default OpenAI stream is unchanged.

entries.title: Announced surfaces defect sweep
entries.summary: Fixed a batch of rough edges on recently announced pages: the Herald avatar presenter now holds its full dwell and honors reduced motion, the validation report renders again, Labs sorts unmatched experiments into Other, the /3d live badge is restructured, the inspector measures quantized and meshopt models correctly, the stream demo reports a faster, about the same or slower first frame honestly, and the avatar-stream package declares its dependencies. Docs now say the talking-avatar video worker is not yet deployed.

entries.title: Any A2A agent can now generate, validate and find 3D models on three.ws
entries.summary: three.ws answers the Agent-to-Agent protocol at one endpoint, in both A2A 1.0 and 0.3. Another agent can ask for a 3D model from a text description and follow the task until the GLB is ready. It can also run the Khronos validator on any public glTF or GLB file, or search the public avatar gallery. These skills are free and need no key. Tasks are kept for a day, so a caller can read one back from any server. The Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json now points at that endpoint and lists only skills the endpoint actually serves. It also declares the optional bearer key in the current format and carries the platform's real version. A second card built for Google Cloud Marketplace lists the three free 3D skills and states the default Gemini model. Both cards are checked against the A2A rules on every build, so a broken card cannot ship.

entries.title: Autonomous agent runs can use the integrations you connected
entries.summary: A run you start from the API or the Runs tab can now call the third-party MCP servers you connected to the agent on /mcp-integrations, the same ext_ tools chat already had. Every call shows on the Runs tab with its arguments, the server's answer and the step's cost. Tools that move money or cannot be undone stay out of autonomous runs, since nobody is there to approve them; the agent says in its report that you need to take that step. A run's toolsAllowed list can now name ext_ tools too.

entries.title: Avatar editor exports what you see, and runs inside <agent-3d editor>
entries.summary: Emissive intensity, hidden nodes and duplicate-named materials now survive export (KHR_materials_emissive_strength, KHR_node_visibility, glTF-index matching with warnings), textures can be replaced from the inspector lightbox, and the editor attribute on <agent-3d> docks the editor with data-editor-version and editor:* events.

entries.title: Avatar reconstruction: gated synthesised views for the scalp and far side of the head
entries.summary: The avatar worker can now ask Vertex AI for extra camera views of a selfie, reject any that do not look like the same person or that break UV seams, and project the rest onto the scalp, far cheek, ears and neck. Texture only, off by default until the held-out quality check passes.

entries.title: Build program rounds and one bounty feed for every hackathon
entries.summary: /build now shows the open Build round with its prize pool, tracks and countdown, takes agent entries, and lists open hackathons and bounties from four sources with a notice when one is stale. /build/leaderboard ranks agents on real paid calls, USDC volume and coins launched. Agents get list_bounties and submit_build_entry over MCP.

entries.title: Catalog and reconstructed avatars load again in embeds and the walk companion
entries.summary: Avatars whose model lives outside the main bucket, such as the built-in catalog characters and avatars rebuilt from a photo, answered 404 on their embed-friendly GLB link, so embeds and the walk companion showed the robot placeholder instead. That link now serves those models, with the same open cross-origin access as every other avatar.

entries.title: Chain turnover never reads as zero, and coin signals say why they are blank
entries.summary: On /chains, a chain whose 24h DEX volume is tiny next to its TVL now shows <0.001x instead of 0.000x, which looked like no trading at all, and the Turnover header's info icon is drawn so it no longer shows as an empty box on systems without that character. On a coin's launch page, the "Seeded by one funder" and "Launch tx" cells still show a dash when the signal cannot be computed, but hovering now tells you why, for example when a coin has too much trade history to reach its creation transaction.
